title: The four kinds of look
summary: Every finish in the catalogue is one of four kinds: a plain base, a base with a pattern, a one-piece special, or a spec-only shine.
what: A base is a material such as gloss, matte, chrome or candy, and it takes the colour you give the zone. A pattern is a shape laid over a base, such as carbon or camo. A one-piece special, called a monolithic, brings its own paint and its own shine together and is made to be used as it comes. A spec-only look, like the Foundation shelf, changes only the shine and keeps your paint colour. Knowing which kind you are holding tells you which controls will matter.
when: You cannot tell why one finish takes your colour and another does not
You are planning a livery and want to know which kind to use where
how: Open the finish picker for a zone.
Look at the card: bases take the zone colour, specials bring their own.
To keep your own colours and change only the shine, set BASE COLOR to Use source paint (spec only).
To add a shape, use the pattern picker on top of the base.

controls.label: BASE COLOR
controls.range: Use finish's own color, Use source paint (spec only), Use solid color, From special, Custom gradient
controls.effect: Chooses where the zone colour comes from.

tips: Specials that bring their own colours (carbon, camo, holographic) will fight a solid colour. Use them as they are.
A base is the best starting point for a custom colour.
pitfalls: A solid colour on a special that brings its own colours can wash the design out.

title: Where a zone gets its colour
summary: BASE COLOR has five choices: the finish own colour, your source paint, a solid colour, colour borrowed from a special, or a gradient.
what: Use finish's own color keeps the colours the finish was made with. Use source paint (spec only) leaves your paint untouched and changes only the shine. Use solid color paints the zone one exact colour, and the app renders that colour as you picked it. From special borrows the colours of a special finish. Custom gradient fades between 2 to 10 colour stops. Under the picker, Lock Base Color keeps your colour when you swap the finish, which is handy for trying many finishes on one colour.
when: Keep my colours, change only the shine
Make this exact colour
Fade from one colour to another
how: Click a zone card, then open the BASE section.
Choose a mode in the BASE COLOR dropdown.
For a solid colour, pick it. For a gradient, add stops and choose a direction.
Tick Lock Base Color to keep the colour when you change finish.

controls.label: Solid color
controls.effect: The exact colour for Use solid color.

controls.label: Custom gradient
controls.range: 2-10 stops; horizontal, vertical, diagonal down, diagonal up, radial, angular

tips: A gradient runs across the flat sheet, so each side of the car may fade differently. Use one zone per side to control it.
pitfalls: Solid colour on a finish that brings its own colours (carbon, camo, holographic) hides what the finish does.
Source paint mode only works if the zone sits over paint you already have.

title: Foundation: shine without repainting
summary: Foundation finishes change only the surface, never your colour. Pick one when you like your paint and just want it glossier, matter or more metallic.
what: The Foundation shelf holds the 25 plain body materials. Their spec is flat within each finish, so there is no grain or flake. That keeps your paint exactly as it is. In the picker, a Foundation pick keeps the source paint. Other metals like Chrome or Candy repaint the car, because they bring their own colour handling. So for a shine-only change, choose a Foundation material.
when: Make it chrome but keep my livery
Make the whole car matte without changing colours
Add pearl or metallic sheen
how: Select the zone.
Open the Base Material picker and open the Foundation shelf.
Pick a material such as Chrome, Satin Chrome, Metallic, Pearl, Brushed, Matte or Satin.
Leave BASE COLOR on source paint and render.

controls.label: BASE COLOR
controls.default: Use source paint on Foundation picks

tips: Measured values (metal, rough, coat): Gel Coat 0, 15, 16. Chrome 255, 2, 16. Satin Chrome 250, 45, 40. Metallic 200, 50, 16. Pearl 100, 40, 16. Brushed 180, 75, 65. Matte 0, 200, 160. Satin 0, 95, 70.
Add texture with a spec overlay, not with the Foundation material.
pitfalls: The plain Chrome, Metallic and Candy bases repaint the car. Use the Foundation versions for shine only.
aliases: make it chrome keep my colors
make it matte keep my colours

title: Which part of a finish does the work
summary: Finishes fall into five groups by where the character lives: in the shine only, in the pattern shape, in an image, in fine colour detail, or in both paint and shine.
what: Spec-driven finishes keep the paint flat and put everything into the shine: Foundation, Clearcoat and Ghost Geometry. Pattern-design finishes are about shape, not colour: carbon, geometric, optical, decades and similar. Pattern-image finishes carry real colour from an image: the Cultural family. Fine structural colour finishes use tiny marks of 8 to 32 pixels whose colour shows through the shine: Fractured Cryptid, Morpho, Bloom and Petri, Neon and ASTRA. Everything else, the bulk of the catalogue, uses both paint and shine.
when: You wonder why recolouring one finish does nothing
You want to predict how a finish will react to your colour
how: Find the finish group in the catalogue.
Spec-driven: choose it for shine and set colour separately.
Pattern-design: choose it for the shape and recolour freely.
Fine structural colour: leave scale alone and judge it on the car.
tips: Classic Foundation has no texture on purpose. Grain and flake belong in patterns and spec overlays.
The Foundation EFX shelf carries its own paint and shine, so it is a full finish, not spec-only.
pitfalls: A fine structural colour finish scaled up loses its effect.

title: How the catalogue is organised
summary: The catalogue holds 4,179 finishes: 1,144 bases and 3,035 specials, grouped into named shelves, plus 319 patterns and 301 spec patterns.
what: Finishes sit on 59 shelves, such as ASTRA, FLAW LAB, SHOKK WORKS, Foundation, Foundation EFX, the retro shelves, the Fractured series and the heritage shelves. Two big shelves collect the rest: More Bases with 449 and More Specials with 1,158. Every finish has a card with a plain description, ratings and best uses. Patterns and spec patterns are separate lists. A finish also belongs to a broader category such as Chrome and Mirror, Candy and Tinted Clear, Carbon and Composite or Weathered and Aged.
when: You want to browse by mood or theme
You want to know how many finishes there are
how: Open the finish library or the Base Material picker.
Pick a shelf or a category.
Use the search box or the hashtag chips to narrow it down.
tips: Shelf sizes: ASTRA 50, FLAW LAB 25, SHOKK WORKS 89, Foundation 25, Foundation EFX 46, Iridescent Insects 50, PRISM FORGE 50, X LAB 50.
Search for a feeling such as "icy" or "rusty" and the finish cards are searched by meaning.
pitfalls: The number 4,799 you may see in reports counts bases, specials, patterns and spec patterns together.

title: Foundation and Foundation EFX
summary: Foundation is the 25 plain body materials. Foundation EFX is 46 materials with a visible effect on top, such as orange peel, damascus steel or gold leaf.
what: Foundation: Wet Look, Gloss, Semi-Gloss, Satin, Eggshell, Matte, Primer, Flat Black, Powder Coat, Pearl, Satin Pearl, Metallic, Matte Metallic, Candy, Brushed, Frozen, Bead Blast, Chrome, Dark Chrome, Satin Chrome and a few specials. They take your zone colour. Foundation EFX adds a surface story on top, like orange peel, wire-brushed metal, damascus steel, gold leaf, snow crust, chalked paint or cast iron, and still takes your colour.
when: You need a clean body material
You want a body material with a hint of character
how: Open the Base Material picker.
Choose Foundation for a clean material or Foundation EFX for an effect.
Set the colour with BASE COLOR.
tips: Start with Foundation and add a spec overlay if you want texture without an EFX look.
pitfalls: EFX finishes bring their own texture. Do not stack another heavy pattern on top.

title: ASTRA: the flagship shelf
summary: ASTRA is a shelf of 50 hero paints with multi-material looks such as nacre, meteorite, chronograph gold and quasicrystal. They are made to be the star of the car.
what: ASTRA finishes bring their own colours and are built from fine detail of 8 to 32 pixels. Colour appears and moves through the shine rather than through bold paint shapes. They look best on a hero area, such as the hood or the side panels, with calmer neighbours.
when: You want one jaw-dropping area
You want luxury without a pattern
how: Open the Base Material picker.
Pick the ASTRA shelf.
Preview a few with See on paint.
Apply it to one hero zone.
tips: Leave the scale alone: the detail is already fine.
Keep neighbours matte or plain so the hero reads.
pitfalls: Putting ASTRA on every zone makes them compete.

title: Ghost Geometry and Clearcoat
summary: These two families keep the paint flat and hide their pattern in the shine, so shapes appear only when the light hits them.
what: Ghost Geometry hides stripes, grids and hexes in the clearcoat. Head on the paint looks plain, and the pattern shows up at angles. The Depth and Geometry shelf has 41 of them, including Depth Map, Ghost Hex Grid and Ghost Stripes. Clearcoat finishes work the same way: spec-driven, flat paint, with the character in the top coat. Because they live in the shine, your paint colour stays yours.
when: You want a subtle look that only shows in the sun
You want to keep stripes and numbers fully readable
how: Open the Depth and Geometry shelf.
Pick a Ghost finish and keep BASE COLOR on your colour.
Check the car at an angle, not head on.
tips: The spec varies across the surface inside each ghost finish, so it is not flat like Foundation.
pitfalls: A ghost finish will look like nothing on a flat template preview.

title: ColorShoxx and colour-shift finishes
summary: ColorShoxx and the chameleon-style shelves give a colour that seems to change as the car moves.
what: ColorShoxx has 25 premium dual-tone and multi-colour shifting finishes. Related shelves: Prizm with 40 chameleon metals, Spectrum Shift with 60 spectral colour pairs, Fractured Nightshift with 50 day and night colour flips, plus the Chameleon, Color Science and Aurora Flow categories. iRacing cannot do a true hue shift, so these use dark paint and fine spec detail that catches the light at angles.
when: You want a chameleon or flip look
You want colour to change between daylight and dusk
how: Pick a shift shelf.
Keep the base dark and the scale fine.
Use COLOR FLIP to move the second colour around the wheel where it is available.

controls.label: COLOR FLIP
controls.effect: 90 gives a neighbouring hue, 180 the opposite.

tips: Judge on the car at distance, with the car turned.
pitfalls: Scaling a shift finish up kills the shift.

title: Fractured, Mortal Shokk and Neon Underground
summary: The Fractured shelves are the largest family of fine, detailed finishes. Mortal Shokk and Neon Underground are two signature series.
what: Fractured shelves: Elements 60, Cosmos 60, Nightshift 50, Flames 75, Minds 55, Souls 30, Forge 88, Opalfire 50, Foundry 50, Tessera 50, Wilds 110, Relics 50 and Shokk 20. Each has a theme, such as weather, space, fire or foundry metal. The Cryptid, Morpho, Bloom and Petri sub-families use micro marks with colour showing through the shine. Mortal Shokk (26 finishes) has 4K plates, each with its own hand-built spec map. Neon Underground (25) is street-racing neon with fine coloured detail.
when: You want a rich themed look at 8 to 32 pixels of detail
You want street neon
how: Open the picker and browse the Fractured shelves.
Pick one close to your theme.
Preview with See on paint before you apply.
tips: Fractured shelves are worth a scan at car scale. The detail is the point, so judge it close.
pitfalls: A big scale value breaks the fine detail.

title: Source plates, X LAB, SHOKK WORKS and PRISM FORGE
summary: These are the hand-made hero shelves: authored image plates, experimental X LAB finishes, engineered SHOKK WORKS specials and PRISM FORGE flake looks.
what: SOURCE PATTERN PLATES (24) are authored pattern images. X LAB (50) holds experimental hero finishes such as Dichroic Skin, Hologram Metal and Abyssal Lens. SHOKK WORKS (89) is engineered specials: foil webs, charge ropes, lightning channels. PRISM FORGE (50) is iridescent and multi-colour flake. FLAW LAB (25) is industrial inspection: etches, stress bands and cracks. IMPOSSIBLE FINISHES (10) are wild one-offs.
when: You want a signature, unusual look
You want something no one else has
how: Open the picker and choose the shelf.
Preview a few.
Use one per car as a hero.
tips: Some X LAB finishes are protected gold standards and never change between versions.
pitfalls: Experimental finishes bring their own colours. A solid colour overrides their look.

title: Retro, decades and heritage shelves
summary: Look here for theme: 50s diner, 60s and 70s psychedelia, 80s and 90s nostalgia, and shelves inspired by Japan, Mexico, Britain, China and America.
what: Retro: FAR OUT 60 (disco, outlaw, 70s), BAD AND RAD 60 (80s and 90s Memphis), ALL THAT 60 (90s nostalgia), Flames 20, Sock Hop 20 (1950s diner) and Groovy Vibes 20 (60s and 70s). Heritage: RISING SUN 52, VIVA MEXICO 58, UNION JACKED 45, FORBIDDEN DRAGON 20, LET FREEDOM RING 10, plus WORLD OF COLOR with 100 country palettes and ANIME INSPIRED with 15. These bring their own colours and mostly sit in satin to gloss.
when: You are building a themed or tribute livery
You want an era look
how: Pick a shelf that matches the theme.
Use the finish as it comes for the colours.
Add numbers and sponsors in a calm area.
tips: Decades patterns are about shape, not colour. Colour them freely.
pitfalls: Heritage finishes bring colours. A solid colour hides them.

title: Nature, tactical and cyberpunk shelves
summary: For earthy, rugged or night-city looks: camo and field gear, weather and organic textures, and rain-slick neon.
what: TACTICAL AND FIELD (60) is camouflage and military matte. FRACTURED WILDS (110) is organic nature micro-worlds. Fractured Elements is weather and earth. Materials and Physics (31) has acid rain and salt spray. Signal (25) is glow sources like neon signs and tesla coils. CYBERPUNK (60) is the rain-slick neon city. DARK CITY (50) is moody dark palettes. The Industrial and Tactical and Atmosphere categories add more.
when: Rugged or military build
Night-city neon
Nature or weather theme
how: Open the picker and choose the shelf.
Use camo as it comes for the colours.
Add spec overlays for dirt or wear.
tips: For a worn camo, pair it with a Weathered and Aged finish on the lower zones.
pitfalls: Camo with a strong pattern on top turns busy fast.

title: The finish picker, library and browser
summary: Three ways to browse: the Base Material picker popup in a zone, the full-screen finish library, and the Finish Catalog browser with compare.
what: The Base Material picker has a search box, hashtag chips (carbon, chrome, metallic, candy, pearl, chameleon, fire, ice, galaxy, matte, gold, neon, glass, crystal, copper, grunge, scales, luxury, tactical, racing, toxic), a Color Lock button, Surprise me, an On-Car Stage and USE IT. See on paint previews the finish on your own paint. The full-screen library has a search box that understands #tags, plus a favourites star. The Finish Catalog browser lists All Types, Base + Pattern, Monolithic, All Bases or All Patterns with sorting by Default, A to Z, Z to A, Recent or Favorites, and a Finish Comparison with a + Column button.
when: You are hunting for a finish
You want to compare two or three finishes side by side
how: In a zone, click the Base Material swatch.
Type a word or click a chip.
Click a finish to put it on the On-Car Stage, then USE IT.
Star the ones you like and use the favourites filter later.

controls.label: Color Lock
controls.effect: Keeps your colour when you change finish.

controls.label: Surprise me
controls.effect: Puts a highly ranked finish on the stage.

controls.label: See on paint
controls.effect: Previews the finish on your paint.

tips: Surprise me is the quickest way to find an unexpected winner.
Keep Color Lock on while you audition finishes on one colour.
pitfalls: A finish may look different on the car than on its swatch. Use See on paint.

title: Finish cards: what each finish says about itself
summary: Every finish has a card with a plain description, mood, era, best uses, ratings and finishes that pair well. The built-in advisor reads the same cards.
what: A card covers 4,799 entries across finishes, patterns and spec patterns. It says what the finish looks like, a list of moods such as aggressive, stealth, luxury, retro, icy or fiery, an era from 50s to futuristic, where it works on a car (body, hood, roof, sides, stripes, numbers, trim, hero panel, bumpers), how loud and how busy it is, and what pairs well or should be avoided. Search finds finishes by meaning, not just by name, and kits suggest a Classic, Premium or Bold plan for the whole car.
when: You need to find a finish by feeling
You want to know what to pair with your hero finish
how: Type a feeling or a use into the search, such as "rugged hood".
Open a result to read the card.
Check the pair and avoid lists before you stack finishes.
tips: Pick one hero finish, then take its paired finishes for the rest of the car.
pitfalls: A loud, busy finish on every zone fights itself.

title: What makes a finish pop
summary: Contrast between neighbours and a spec that is the colour-opposite of the paint make a finish pop. Saturation alone does not.
what: The best looking cars have one loud hero area, fine texture, and neighbours that contrast in temperature and in surface. Warm matte beside cool metal reads as two materials. Readability matters: iRacing is seen at speed and at distance, so numbers and sponsors need a calm area. A paint file is limited, so choose a few strong ideas and do them well.
when: Your car looks flat
You are choosing between two finishes
how: Choose a hero zone.
Give neighbours the opposite surface and temperature.
Keep numbers and sponsors on plain areas.
Check the car at a distance.
tips: Finish by goal: hood for hero, sides for stripes and numbers, roof calm.
See Paint and spec work together for the technical side.
pitfalls: More saturation is not more pop.

title: Base strength, hue, saturation and brightness
summary: Four sliders tune the zone colour after you choose a finish: BASE STRENGTH, HUE SHIFT, SATURATION and BRIGHTNESS.
what: BASE STRENGTH fades the whole base look over your source paint: 0 is your original paint, 100 percent is the full finish. HUE SHIFT turns every colour around the wheel from -180 to 180 degrees. SATURATION runs from -100 (greyer) to 100 (more vivid). BRIGHTNESS runs from -100 (darker) to 200 (brighter). Each has a reset arrow.
when: The colour is almost right
You want a hint of the finish instead of full coverage
how: Select the zone and open BASE.
Drag BASE STRENGTH down to let your paint through.
Use HUE SHIFT, SATURATION and BRIGHTNESS to tune the colour.

controls.label: BASE STRENGTH
controls.effect: Fades the finish over your paint.

tips: For shine only, use SPEC STRENGTH instead of BASE STRENGTH.
pitfalls: Lowering BASE STRENGTH also lowers colour changes, not just shine.

title: Colour scale, depth, flip and underglow
summary: Four sliders shape how colour sits in a finish: COLOR SCALE, COLOR DEPTH, COLOR FLIP and UNDERGLOW. They unlock after you pick a colour mode.
what: COLOR DEPTH (0 to 100, steps of 5) is candy-coat depth: low is a thin glaze, high is deep wet candy. COLOR FLIP (0 to 355) rotates the dark structure of the paint to a second hue, like a chameleon, with 90 giving a neighbouring hue and 180 the opposite. UNDERGLOW (0 to 100) lets a metal ground coat shine through: gold under warm colours, silver under cool ones. COLOR SCALE and COLOR ROTATION zoom and turn a gradient or borrowed colour art. These stay locked until BASE COLOR is solid, gradient or from special. For ready-made fades, the Gradients (43), Gradient Directional (34), Color Clash (25) and Gradient Extended (101) shelves hold finished gradients and vortexes.
when: You want a candy look
You want a two-tone flip
how: Set BASE COLOR to Use solid color, Custom gradient or From special.
Drag COLOR DEPTH for candy.
Drag COLOR FLIP for a second hue.
Drag UNDERGLOW for metal shimmer.

controls.label: COLOR FLIP
controls.effect: Second hue for a flip look.

controls.label: COLOR SCALE and ROTATION
controls.range: scale and rotation of the colour art

tips: Plain solid colours render exactly as picked until you touch these sliders.
pitfalls: Touching Color Depth darkens an exact colour. Leave it alone if you want the exact colour.

title: Base scale and rotation
summary: BASE SCALE sets how big the finish texture is and BASE ROTATION turns it. Smaller is finer, with more repeats.
what: Base scale runs from 0.05 to 5.0 times, with 1.00 at the centre of the slider. Rotation runs from 0 to 355 degrees in steps of 5. It scales the texture of the finish, not its colours and not the whole car. Because the canvas is the whole car, carbon, flake and camo often look huge at 1.00. Going below 1.00 gives the fine detail that reads as premium. Spec follows base scale until you tick INDEPENDENT SPEC.
when: Carbon, flake or camo looks too large
The texture runs the wrong way
how: Select the zone and open BASE.
Drag BASE SCALE below 1.00 for finer.
Drag BASE ROTATION to turn.
tips: When someone says "crushed to 50%" they mean the scale.
pitfalls: Scaling a fine structural colour finish up weakens it.

title: Second base and overlays
summary: A zone can stack a second to fifth base finish over the first, with a blend mode, to build two-layer looks like chrome flake over candy.
what: In the OVERLAYS section click Add 3rd overlay and so on to open the next slot. Each overlay has its own finish, colour, strength and scale. There are ten blend modes: Fractal Dust, Pattern Edges, Pattern-Reactive, Pattern-Pop, Tint (subtle), Pattern Peaks, Pattern Glow, Pattern Fresnel, Pattern Flow and Pattern Shatter. Overlay scale only affects the fractal and dust modes. Overlays also have hue, saturation and brightness.
when: Chrome flake over candy
Matte clear on gloss
how: Open OVERLAYS in the zone.
Pick a second finish.
Choose a blend mode.
Lower its strength until it sits right.
tips: Start with Tint (subtle) at a low strength.
pitfalls: Every overlay adds render time and visual noise.

title: Wear: scuffed and aged looks
summary: Wear is a stored per-zone value from 0 to 100 that the engine turns into chips, scratches and a duller clearcoat. This build has no Wear slider and Season mode is retired, so you get a worn look from a worn Base Material and Base Strength.
what: Wear is a number from 0 to 100 kept on each zone. When a zone has wear above 0, the render engine adds chips, scratches and a duller clearcoat to that zone. In this build nothing in the Pro window sets it: the zone card has no Wear slider, and the old Season set-up (add races, Quick: Wear Ramp, Render All Races) is retired. Its panel stays hidden and nothing opens it. To get a worn look today, pick a worn finish as the zone's Base Material, lower Base Strength so your own paint shows through, and add chip or scuff spec overlays.
when: A race-worn, barn-find or sun-faded look
You wonder where the Wear slider and Season mode went
how: Make or pick the zone to age: Remaining on Car Paint, or APPLY AREA > Draw box on the lower body, front or roof.
Under BASE press Base Material and search a worn finish: Sun Faded, Die-Back Patina, Hardware: Battle Worn or Surface Rust.
Lower Base Strength to 50 to 70 so your own colours show through (0 is your paint, 100 is the full finish).
For chips and scuffs open BASE > SPEC OVERLAYS and add Micro Chipping or Scuffed Enamel at Strength 30 to 40.
Press RENDER and check at 100 percent zoom: wear should read as fine detail, not blotches.

controls.label: Base Strength
controls.effect: How much of the worn finish replaces your own paint.

tips: Sun Faded and Surface Rust are on the Foundation EFX shelf, Die-Back Patina on SHOKK WORKS and Hardware: Battle Worn on TACTICAL & FIELD, so searching by name is quickest.
Desert Worn, Barn Find and Rally Mud exist in the catalogue but are not listed in the Base Material picker. Ask the Shokker AI helper for them by name.
pitfalls: High Base Strength with a heavy worn finish hides your own colours and fine detail.
